title: Follow-ups from frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize's PR #373 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #373 (frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges. The PR's blocking finding (missing focus trap in the maximized overlay) is tracked on the parent task's own `review.comments`/re-opened checklist, not here -- this file is only the non-blocking items.

checklist.step: common/ChartFrame's drag-to-resize handle (role="separator" at ChartFrame.tsx ~line 271) has no keyboard equivalent at all: it has no `tabIndex`, isn't reachable via Tab, and has no `onKeyDown` handler. Confirmed via real-browser walkthrough (Tab from the maximize toggle skips straight past the handle to the next MetricHelp button). Per the WAI-ARIA separator/window-splitter pattern, an interactive separator should be focusable (`tabIndex={0}`) and support ArrowUp/ArrowDown to adjust the height, with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` reflecting the current/clamped height. Non-blocking because the full-screen toggle (a real, keyboard-accessible `<button>`) already gives keyboard users an alternative way to see the chart bigger, but the resize affordance itself is currently mouse/touch-only, which is a real WCAG 2.1.1 gap worth closing.

No per-component (vitest/Testing Library) test asserts the maximize-toggle/drag-resize wiring specifically for OscillatorChart, VolumeIndicatorsChart, or TrendStrengthChart -- only ChartFrame's own generic unit tests (against a synthetic test double) and one e2e spec scoped to PriceChart exercise this interaction against real component code. The three other panes' wiring (passing `canvasHeight` into their own chart-container `Box`, placing `maximizeToggle` in their own title row) is currently verified only by my own manual real-browser walkthrough during PR #373's review, not by anything that runs on every future change. Add either a lightweight render-time assertion per component (maximize toggle renders, clicking it doesn't throw, canvas height prop reflects `canvasHeight`) or extend the e2e spec to touch at least one of the other three panes.

`ChartFrame.tsx`'s `MAXIMIZED_CHROME_ALLOWANCE_PX = 220` is a single constant shared across all four panes despite their chrome (controls/legend rows above the canvas) differing materially -- PriceChart's range/interval ToggleButtonGroups plus several MetricHelp legend rows are taller than Oscillators/VolumeIndicators/TrendStrength's single title row. The maximized overlay's own `overflow: 'auto'` is the documented fallback if the real chrome exceeds the estimate, and this held up fine in manual testing at a 900px-tall viewport, but wasn't checked at a smaller viewport height (e.g. a ~700px laptop screen) where PriceChart's taller chrome could push more of the canvas below the fold inside the maximized view. Worth a real-browser check at a shorter viewport.

Flagged by an independent high-effort code-review pass against the same PR #373 diff: `ChartFrame.tsx`'s window-resize `useSyncExternalStore` subscription (`subscribeToWindowResize`/`computeMaximizedHeight`, ~line 186) stays active for the component's entire lifetime regardless of `isMaximized`, so every browser resize/orientation-change re-renders all four (legend/MetricHelp-heavy) chart panes even while none is maximized and the recomputed `maximizedHeight` is immediately discarded by `canvasHeight`'s non-maximized branch. Minor render-churn cost, not a correctness bug -- worth gating the subscription on `isMaximized` (or otherwise avoiding the unconditional re-render) if it shows up in practice.

Found during PR #373's round-2 re-review (the needs_work fix for the focus trap/scroll-lock stacking, independently confirmed by a code-review pass that ran the component under vitest/jsdom to compare round-1 vs round-2 behavior): the new Tab-trap scopes 'inside the dialog' purely to `frameRef`'s own DOM subtree, which doesn't account for a portaled MUI component (a `Popover`/`Menu`/`Autocomplete`) opened from content *inside* the maximized overlay -- e.g. a `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` '?' popover used throughout `PriceChart`/`OscillatorChart`/`VolumeIndicatorsChart`/`TrendStrengthChart`. Verified (real browser + a vitest/jsdom reproduction): opening such a popover while maximized and pressing Tab does NOT escape focus anywhere (MUI's own `Modal`/`enforceFocus` wins the resulting tug-of-war and keeps focus on the popover's own Paper every time, and Escape still correctly closes just the popover first, then the dialog on a second press -- no observable defect with any of this app's actual current content). Non-blocking today specifically because every current `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` instance used inside these four chart panes (`metricHelpContent.ts`'s registry, the divergence-marker balloon) renders plain `Typography` text with zero interactive elements -- confirmed by grepping for `Button`/`<a `/`Link`/`onClick` in that content, none found. Would become a real keyboard-reachability bug the moment any such popover's content ever gained an interactive element (a button, a link) inside it: that element would become permanently unreachable via Tab while the popover is open, since the outer trap's blind 'redirect anything outside frameRef back inside' logic doesn't know to defer to a nested modal's own focus management. Worth hardening `ChartFrame`'s Tab handler to recognize when `document.activeElement` is inside some OTHER already-open modal/popover root (e.g. check for an ancestor with `role="dialog"`/`.MuiPopover-root`/`.MuiModal-root` other than its own `frameRef`) and no-op in that case, deferring entirely to that nested modal's own focus handling.

Found during PR #373's round-2 re-review (same code-review pass as the nested-popover finding above): `ChartFrame.tsx`'s focus trap is per-instance only (each maximized instance's own `window`-level `keydown` listener only knows its own `frameRef`), with no coordination across multiple simultaneously-maximized instances -- unlike the sibling body-scroll-lock fix in this same PR, which explicitly uses a shared module-level counter for exactly this multi-instance case. If two `ChartFrame` instances are ever both maximized at once (confirmed unreachable today via an ordinary mouse click -- a real, actionability-checked Playwright click on a background pane's maximize button times out because the foreground overlay's `position: fixed; inset: 0` genuinely intercepts the pointer event at the browser's own hit-testing level, not just visually -- and unreachable via keyboard Tab alone now that the first blocking finding is fixed), each instance's Tab listener treats focus sitting in the *other* instance as 'escaped my dialog' and both independently fight to redirect it back into themselves on every Tab press (confirmed via code reading: neither listener calls `stopPropagation`). In practice this resolves to the most-recently-opened (topmost) instance winning every time, purely because its `useEffect` registers its `window` listener later and therefore runs last for the same bubbling event -- not because of any deliberate coordination -- meaning Tab navigation becomes unusable in the earlier-opened instance for as long as the later one stays open. A related, more concerning reachability path: `ChartFrame` doesn't apply `aria-hidden`/`inert` to the rest of the page while maximized (unlike MUI's own `Modal`/`ModalManager`, which does this specifically for assistive-technology isolation), so a screen-reader user in a virtual-cursor/browse-mode workflow could potentially activate a background pane's own maximize button directly through the accessibility tree (bypassing both the visual z-index occlusion and the Tab-key interception, neither of which virtual-cursor navigation goes through) and reach this same two-simultaneously-maximized, dueling-focus-trap state through an ordinary assistive-technology workflow rather than only a synthetic script-driven one -- this part not independently confirmed against a real screen reader in this review (no AT available in this environment), so its real-world reachability is plausible but unverified. Worth considering `aria-hidden` on `ChartFrame`'s maximized-overlay siblings (mirroring what `Dialog`/`Modal` would have provided for free, per this PR's own decisions entry on what was and wasn't reimplemented) and/or a shared cross-instance registry for the focus trap akin to the existing `acquireBodyScrollLock` counter, if this component is ever used somewhere multiple instances can legitimately be open at once.

decisions.decision: Resolved the drag-to-resize keyboard-equivalent item (checklist item 1) directly on the parent task `frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize` during its needs_work re-review round (PR #373), folded in alongside the two blocking fixes rather than deferred to this followups task's own later pass. The other three checklist items here remain open/untouched.
decisions.rationale: The parent task's own `decisions` entry explains why this specific finding (not the other three) was the one worth folding in now: it was the cheapest, most self-contained addition to a file already being changed for the two blocking fixes, and closing a real WCAG 2.1.1 gap was judged worth the small amount of extra surface area in that same PR. See `frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize.json`'s `decisions` array for the implementation details (tabIndex, aria-valuenow/min/max, Arrow/Home/End key handling) and its own test coverage.

decisions.decision: Added 3 new non-blocking checklist items during PR #373's round-2 re-review (the needs_work fix for the two original blocking findings): a nested-portaled-modal Tab-swallowing gap, a per-instance (uncoordinated) focus trap for a hypothetical two-simultaneously-maximized state, and the related missing `aria-hidden`/`inert` on background content while maximized. Judged non-blocking rather than sending the PR back a third time: both the original round-1 blocking findings (Tab/Shift+Tab escaping the maximized overlay to reach another pane's own maximize button; body-scroll-lock restore breaking across two out-of-order-closed simultaneous instances) were independently re-verified fixed in a real browser for their exact originally-reported reproductions, and none of these 3 new findings has a live reachable defect against this app's actual current content/interaction surface today (confirmed: no `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` instance inside any of the four chart panes has interactive content for the nested-popover gap to bite on; a real, actionability-checked Playwright click cannot reach a background pane's maximize button while another is maximized, since the foreground overlay's `position: fixed` genuinely intercepts the pointer event at the browser's hit-testing level, not just visually, so the dueling-focus-trap/no-aria-hidden findings require either future content changes or an unverified assistive-technology workflow to manifest).
decisions.rationale: The project's own established precedent from this same task's round-1 review was to escalate a newly-found issue to blocking specifically when it was directly, concretely reachable via an already-confirmed live bug (the scroll-lock finding was escalated because it was 'reachable via the focus-trap gap' that existed at the time) -- these 3 new findings don't meet that bar: two require content this app doesn't currently have, and the third (missing aria-hidden/inert) is a real and legitimate hardening gap relative to what MUI's own Modal/ModalManager would have provided for free, but its practical reachability depends on specific assistive-technology/browser aria-modal support this review had no way to test, making it a genuinely arguable rather than clear-cut severity call. Tracking all three here (rather than silently dropping them, or blocking the PR on speculative/unverified severity) keeps them visible for whoever next touches this component, consistent with this file's whole purpose.

decisions.decision: Closed the three clearly-actionable checklist items (per-component maximize/resize tests, the `MAXIMIZED_CHROME_ALLOWANCE_PX` shorter-viewport investigation, and gating the window-resize subscription on `isMaximized`) in this pass; deferred the remaining three (nested-portaled-popover Tab-swallowing, uncoordinated per-instance focus traps, missing `aria-hidden`/`inert` on background content) as speculative accessibility hardening with no live defect today, per the dispatch's own explicit framing. Added 2 vitest/Testing Library tests per component to `OscillatorChart.test.tsx`/`VolumeIndicatorsChart.test.tsx`/`TrendStrengthChart.test.tsx` (maximize-toggle-into-and-out-of-the-dialog-with-the-real-canvas-visible-inside-it, and drag-resize-via-pointer-events-changing-the-real-container's-height) -- exercising the real component code's own wiring (not ChartFrame's synthetic test double), closing the gap the round-1/round-2 reviews both flagged. Investigated `MAXIMIZED_CHROME_ALLOWANCE_PX=220` via a real-browser Playwright walkthrough (throwaway script, not committed) against a freshly-started `make backend`/`make frontend` pair on `/stocks/AAPL` (the tallest-chrome pane -- PriceChart's own range/interval controls): maximized Price chart and measured the real chart-container's own bounding box against the viewport at 900px/700px/600px tall -- 99.6%/99.5%/99.3% of the canvas stayed within the viewport without scrolling at every tested height (the fixed ~222.6px measured chrome height is almost exactly the 220px constant), with only ~2-3px of the tallest-chrome pane cut off at the shortest (600px) height tested, fully covered by the overlay's existing `overflow: 'auto'` fallback. Did not chase an even shorter viewport (e.g. 320-400px, closer to a phone held in landscape) after the backend's own `/history` endpoint (FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED=true in this dev environment, unrelated to this task, left untouched per this task's own standing constraint) repeatedly took 50-60+ seconds or timed out per real network round-trip during that investigation, making further real-browser passes impractically slow for a documentation-only follow-up with no evidence so far of a real problem; judged the three already-tested heights sufficient to call this one acceptable as-is rather than needing a code fix. Fixed the window-resize-subscription-stays-active-regardless-of-isMaximized item directly in `ChartFrame.tsx`: wrapped `subscribeToWindowResize` in a `useCallback`-memoized `subscribe` function that only installs the real `window` `resize` listener while `isMaximized` is true (a shared `noopUnsubscribe` otherwise), relying on `useSyncExternalStore`'s own re-subscribe-when-the-subscribe-function's-identity-changes behavior to attach/detach the real listener exactly on each maximize/un-maximize transition; added 2 new ChartFrame.test.tsx tests asserting the real listener is absent while not maximized and is added/removed exactly once across a maximize/un-maximize cycle (via `vi.spyOn(window, 'addEventListener'/'removeEventListener')`).
decisions.rationale: The three items closed here were exactly the ones the dispatch itself called out as clearly worthwhile (concrete, scoped, low-risk) versus the other three being 'genuinely low-priority/speculative given the no-live-defect-today framing' -- both round-1 and round-2 PR #373 reviews already independently confirmed none of the three deferred items has a live reachable defect against this app's actual current content/interaction surface (no MetricHelp/InfoBalloon/AnchoredInfoBalloon instance has interactive content for the nested-popover gap to bite on; two-simultaneously-maximized-instances is unreachable via both mouse -- the foreground overlay's position:fixed genuinely intercepts the pointer event at the browser's hit-testing level -- and keyboard -- the focus trap itself prevents Tabbing to it; the aria-hidden/inert gap's reachability depends on an unverified real-screen-reader workflow this environment has no way to test), and nothing about implementing the three items that WERE closed changed that analysis for the three that weren't. Per-component tests: a lightweight render-time assertion (per the checklist item's own suggested shape) was chosen over extending the e2e spec to a second pane, since vitest/Testing Library tests run far faster and in the same suite already exercising each component's own mocked-lightweight-charts setup, and the e2e spec already covers PriceChart end-to-end against a real browser/real backend -- a second e2e case would mostly duplicate ChartFrame's own interaction mechanics (already covered generically) without adding meaningfully more real-browser-specific coverage than a second vitest assertion would for the wiring question this item is actually about (does THIS component's own JSX correctly plumb canvasHeight/maximizeToggle/resizeHandle into its own markup). MAXIMIZED_CHROME_ALLOWANCE_PX: documented as acceptable rather than refactored into a per-pane constant, since the real-browser measurement showed the existing single constant already tracks the tallest pane's real chrome height almost exactly (222.6px measured vs 220px constant) -- a per-pane constant would mostly matter for PriceChart specifically needing MORE headroom than the other three panes' shorter chrome, but the shared overflow:auto fallback already handles that pane's worst case acceptably (sub-3px clipped at a 600px viewport), so splitting the constant would add maintenance surface (four constants to keep in sync with four panes' chrome, which could itself drift as any pane's controls/legend rows change) without a demonstrated problem to justify it. Window-resize gating: `useCallback`+a conditional no-op unsubscribe was chosen over, e.g., moving the whole subscription inside the existing maximize `useEffect` (which already gates on `isMaximized`), because `useSyncExternalStore` needs its own subscribe/getSnapshot pair to stay the source of truth for `maximizedHeight` -- folding the resize listener into the unrelated focus-trap/scroll-lock effect would couple two independent concerns (keyboard/focus management vs. viewport-height tracking) into one effect for no benefit, where the smaller, targeted `useCallback` change keeps `useSyncExternalStore`'s existing shape and lets React's own re-subscribe-on-subscribe-identity-change machinery do the attach/detach work, with no new effect or manual cleanup bookkeeping to get wrong.
